head: 05d151914cab2f8b1f09dee95f5972e8080d6f4d
summary:
The only deliverable is .taad/fitness.yaml, committed in 05d1519. Nothing under src/ or tests/ changed (`git diff --stat 12763aa HEAD -- src tests` is empty). The file has a single top-level `rules:` key and 8 must_not_match entries, one per (Fact, scope glob) pair. Each entry is rooted, has `including_comments: true` and uses single-quoted regexes. I diffed every pattern against its xUnit literal with a script: all 8 entries equal the ArchitectureRulesTests.cs literal plus a leading `(?m)`, with 0 differences. The Fitness MCP tool, the one validate uses, run in this worktree (which has obj/ and the 770 MB .dotnet/ present) reports '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.', with no unmatched rules. op=rules lists all 8 entries with \b and \s intact. The engine CLI gives the same text. The project's full suite passes 86/86 on the worktree.

In a scratch copy I re-ran the planted shapes against the engine's fitness.check, and each fired on the right entry:
- a line-1 using
- a block-comment DllImport
- UseWPF in Core.csproj
- IsReparsePoint in a .xaml
- FileAttributes.ReparsePoint and 0x00000400 in App .cs
- Skip= and Explicit=true in CancellationTests.cs
- a two-line Skip, which only Fitness catches

Tokens added to the exempted Kernel32.cs still pass. The committed taad3.design._append_rules also appended a 9th rule and left the original bytes as an unchanged prefix, and the check still passed.

One shape not on the matrix was found and measured. A UTF-8-BOM file with `using System.Windows;` on line 1 passes Fitness while xUnit fails it at :1. The cause is the engine reading files with encoding="utf-8": the BOM stays in the text, and Python's \s does not match it. That makes the file header's claim that both engines "fail on the same files" false. No file in the tree has a BOM today, and the xUnit twin still catches the case, so this is minor and does not block the slice. The one declared deviation (the `**/` in the csproj glob) holds: the glob matches FsAnalyser.Core.csproj and op=check reports no unmatched rules. The index shows one build attempt, so there is no loop.

findings.claim: The two TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen entries let a using directive on LINE 1 of a UTF-8-BOM file pass in Fitness, while the xUnit twin fails it. The engine opens covered files with encoding="utf-8" (taad3/fitness.py:422), which keeps U+FEFF as the first character. `(?m)^\s*using` cannot step over it, because Python's \s does not match U+FEFF, and no other ^ position comes before line 1's text. .NET File.ReadAllLines strips the BOM, so xUnit matches. Every Core file that starts with `using` has it on line 1, so line 1 is exactly where this violation would appear. This also makes the yaml header's claim (lines 13-15, 'Both fail on the same files; only that line number can differ') false. The same holds for a UTF-16 file: Fitness decoded it with errors='replace' and matched nothing. I measured only the Fitness side of that case. Nothing in the tree has a BOM today and there is no .editorconfig, so this bites only when an editor saves a file with a BOM. The xUnit test remains the backstop.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:37 and :47 (`(?m)^\s*using\s+(static\s+)?(System\.Windows|...)`); taad_v3 backend/taad3/fitness.py:422 `open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")`. Measured in the scratch copy %TEMP%\sl022-review\tree. Engine fitness.check on Scanner.cs prefixed with EF BB BF + `using System.Windows;\r\n` gave verdict=pass with 0 violations. The same plant without a BOM failed at :1. With the BOM and a second using on line 2, it failed at :2. `dotnet test --no-build --filter ArchitectureRulesTests` on the same planted tree: TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen FAIL at `src\FsAnalyser.Core\Scanning\Scanner.cs:1`.
findings.fix: In both TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen entries, write `(?m)^﻿?\s*using\s+(static\s+)?(System\.Windows|PresentationFramework|FsAnalyser\.App)`, and add 'optional ﻿ after ^' to the header's list of allowed transforms. Measured: the clean tree still passes on 33 files, and the BOM and no-BOM line-1 plants both fail at :1. Alternatively, correct the header sentence to name BOM and UTF-16 files as a known divergence. The durable fix is engine-side: encoding="utf-8-sig" at fitness.py:422.

obligations.evidence: A script parsed each [Fact]'s @"..." pattern literals out of tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs:13-72 and compared them with .taad/fitness.yaml. For all 8 entries the must_not_match list equals the xUnit literals with a `(?m)` prefix, 0 differences. No pattern contains `'` or `$`, and the test compiles with RegexOptions.Multiline only (line 85), so no other transform applies.

The Fitness MCP op=check in the SL-022 worktree reported '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.' with no MATCHED NO FILES section. Engine fitness.check on the scratch copy gave unmatched=[]. The csproj glob `src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.csproj` compiles to `(?:[^/]+/)*` (fitness.py:201-203) and so matches the csproj sitting directly in its folder.

.taad/fitness.yaml:33 has `rules:` as the only top-level key, with 2-space-indented mappings. fitness.load (fitness.py:289-318) requires exactly that, and MCP op=rules listed all 8 entries. The committed design._append_rules (design.py:1037-1067) appends `  # settled by ...` plus 2-space-indented entries at end of file. Run on the scratch copy, the file then loaded 9 rules.

In %TEMP%\sl022-review\tree I called taad3.design._append_rules(root, [Probe rule], 'SL-999'). fitness.load returned 9 rules, the original file bytes were an unchanged prefix of the new file, and fitness.check passed on 33 files with 0 unmatched. The file was restored afterwards.

`git -C taad_v3 grep -n 'def _append_rules' HEAD -- backend/taad3/design.py` gives HEAD:backend/taad3/design.py:1037 at 0260e7e. `git status --short` on design.py and fitness.py in taad_v3 is empty, so the code is committed and not a working-tree edit.

`git check-ignore -v -n --no-index .taad/fitness.yaml` gives `::` (no rule matches), and the same holds for `.taad` and `.taad/new-file.yaml`. The file is tracked (`git ls-files .taad/fitness.yaml`, commit 05d1519), and the untracked .taad/slices/SL-022/build-slice-1.json shows as `??`, not ignored. .gitignore lists only .dotnet/, bin/, obj/, artifacts/, TestResults/, .vs/ and *.user.

cases.evidence: No project test covers this. I ran the Fitness MCP op=rules on the worktree: it lists 8 entries with `0x0*400\b`, `\s*` and `\bExplicit` intact, so the file loaded. The builder's controls (double-quoted \b silently passes, double-quoted \s is refused) were not re-run.
`git check-ignore -v -n --no-index .taad/fitness.yaml` gives no match. The file is committed in 05d1519.

Scratch plants run with the engine's fitness.check: `using System.Windows;` on line 1 fails at :1. With a BOM, a second-line using fails at :2. The builder's P01a at Scanner.cs:7 is reported at :6, a declared line-number offset. A BOM-prefixed line-1 using is NOT caught (see m1).
Scratch plant `/* DllImport */` appended to Scanner.cs fails InteropLivesOnlyInNative (src) at :218. The builder's P02a/P02b used // comments.
Scratch plants: `<UseWPF>true</UseWPF>` in src/FsAnalyser.Core/FsAnalyser.Core.csproj fails the (*.csproj) entry at :13. `<!-- IsReparsePoint -->` in MainWindow.xaml fails the (*.xaml) entry at :48.
Scratch plants in src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs: `FileAttributes.ReparsePoint` and `0x00000400` each fail OnlyTheClassifierReadsTheReparseAttribute (*.cs) at :317.

The clean tree passes with Kernel32.cs and EntryClassifier.cs holding the tokens. A scratch plant adding `DllImport IsReparsePoint 0x400` to Native/Kernel32.cs still passes. The builder's except_files-removed control showed each exemption is needed.

ArchitectureRulesTests.cs is covered by the (tests) interop entry and the never-skipped entry, both with including_comments: true. The MCP op=check passes on it. Its literals (`(Library|Dll)Import`, `Skip(?:Exception)`) do not self-match, so no exemption is needed, and the xUnit test does not exclude itself either.

The MCP op=check shows no MATCHED NO FILES section, and engine unmatched=[] on the scratch copy. The csproj entry covers FsAnalyser.Core.csproj: the planted UseWPF fired on it. The builder's typo control was not re-run.

The MCP op=check on the worktree ran with .dotnet/ (770 MB) and src/tests obj/ present, and read 33 files, the same count as the clean scratch copy. The WPF *.g.cs and LibraryImports.g.cs part rests on the builder's built scratch copy and was not re-run.

This is a declared no-op, and the reason still holds: no pattern in .taad/fitness.yaml contains `$`. The engine also opens files in text mode (fitness.py:422), which normalises CRLF, so even a `$` pattern would match.

Scratch plants in tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CancellationTests.cs: `[Fact(Skip = "no")]`, `[Fact(Explicit = true)]` and a two-line `[Fact(` / `Skip = "x")]` each fail CountingRuleTestsAreNeverSkipped. xUnit misses the two-line form, and Fitness catches it.
Marked non-material by the design. Nothing in this repo branches on it, and the reason (Fitness reads only the slice worktree) still holds.

Marked non-material, but exercised anyway on the scratch copy with the committed design._append_rules: 8 rules became 9 and the original bytes stayed as the prefix. The check still passed on 33 files with 0 unmatched.

drift: The only departure from the design, the `**/` in `src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.csproj`, was declared by the builder and is correct: fitness.py:201-203 lets `**/` match zero directories.

The yaml header (lines 13-15) says the two engines 'fail on the same files; only that line number can differ'. That is broader than what holds. Besides BOM and UTF-16 files (m1), Fitness prunes directories named packages, dist, target, .venv and similar anywhere under src/ and tests/ (fitness.py:325-327, 408), while xUnit's Files() excludes only bin and obj. A file under such a directory is therefore read by xUnit and not by Fitness. Nothing in the tree has such a directory.

Each split entry carries its [Fact]'s full except_files list, including the entries that cannot apply to its scope: TestNative.cs in the (src) interop entry, Native/** in the (tests) entry, and .cs exemptions on the (*.xaml) entry. The header states this, the design did not, and it is harmless.
